full_judgment:
2. All the writ petitions have been filed challenging the judgment and decree of the Land Survey Tribunal of different districts passed in the respective land survey suits. Although section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act ("SAT Act") incorporates provisions for challenging judgment and decree of the Land Survey Tribunal by preferring appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal but at the relevant time of passing those decrees, there was no appellate forum due to which the petitioners of the respective writ petitions being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree, filed these writ petitions and obtained the Rules Nisi. 

 6. Section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as "the SAT Act") incorporates the provisions regarding appeal against the judgment and decree or order of the Land Survey Tribunal. The same are as follows: 

 11. From the facts, it appears that although at the time of enactment of section 145B of the SAT Act in 2004, the Statute incorporated the provisions for preferring appeal within 3 months from the date of decree or order but the forum of appeal for the first time established by the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2023 Gazetted on 7-6-2023 and by the Gazette Notification dated 23-8-2023, the jurisdiction of Land Survey Appellate Tribunal has been determined under different districts. In the circumstances, since the appellate forum has been established on 23-8-2023, we are of the view that the petitioners can take their grievances to the respective Land Survey Appellate Tribunals by preferring appeal challenging the impugned judgment and decree or order. 

 "We have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in both the cases and perused the impugned judgment and orders of the High Court Division as well as other materials on record. Upon perusal it appears that section 145B of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 stipulates 3 (three) months' time for preferring appeal before the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal. 

 "Meanwhile status quo in respect of possession of the suit land shall continue till 3 (three) months from the date of establishment of the Land Survey Appellate Tribunal or from the date of empowering the District Judge as the Judge of the concerned Land Survey Appellate Tribunal under. section 145B(3A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (as amended in 2023)"
